name: Test

on:
  # We want to run the CI when anything is pushed to master.
  # Since master is a protected branch this only happens when a PR is merged.
  # This is a double check in case the PR was stale and had some issues.
  push:
    branches:
      - master
    paths-ignore: # Prevents from running if only docs are updated
      - 'doc/**'
      - '**/*README*'
      - '**.md'
      - '**.rst'
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore: # Prevents from running if only docs are updated
      - 'doc/**'
      - '**/*README*'
      - '**.md'
      - '**.rst'
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
  - cron: '0 0 * * *' # daily

# We want to cancel previous runs for a given PR or branch / ref if another CI
# run is requested.
# See: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-jobs/using-concurrency
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  # default compiler for all non-compatibility tests
  MATRIX_EVAL: "CC=gcc-13 && CXX=g++-13"
  # install_apt_packages.sh installs the apt packages. Jobs that build the GUI
  # additionally run dev/ensure_qt6_sdk.sh to provision a Qt6 SDK (>= the
  # supported floor). CMake discovers Qt and bakes its location into the
  # binaries, so no CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH or runtime Qt env is needed anywhere.

jobs:
  BuildVTR:
    name: 'B: Building VTR Release'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      with:
        submodules: 'true'

    - name: Get number of CPU cores
      uses: SimenB/github-actions-cpu-cores@v3
      id: cpu-cores

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: ./install_apt_packages.sh

    - uses: hendrikmuhs/ccache-action@v1.2.24
      with:
        key: ${{ github.job }}

    - name: Build
      env:
        CMAKE_PARAMS: "-DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=on -DVTR_IPO_BUILD=off -DVTR_ASSERT_LEVEL=3"
        BUILD_TYPE: release
        NUM_PROC: ${{ steps.cpu-cores.outputs.count }}
      run: |
        export PATH="/usr/lib/ccache:/usr/local/opt/ccache/libexec:$PATH"
        make -j${{ steps.cpu-cores.outputs.count}}

    # Here we pack the build to store it as a build artifact. We exclude specific files
    # to keep the build artifact reasonably low (to speed up file download times in the
    # CI). Beyond the executables, some files need to be kept such as CTestTestFile.cmake
    # files which are used by the unit tests CI run.
    - name: Pack Build
      shell: bash
      run: |
        tar -czvf build.tar.gz --exclude='CMakeFiles' --exclude='*.a' --exclude='cmake_install.cmake' build/

    - name: Store Build Artifact
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: build-release.tar.gz
        path: build.tar.gz
        retention-days: 1

    name: 'B: Building VTR Release With Odin'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

results.content:
Cancel superseded runs

Pattern: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (stale_run_cancellation)

When is cancel superseded runs applicable?

Assess cancel superseded runs for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR; A newer revision supersedes older checks

Contraindications: Release or deployment work; Distinct branches share a cancellation group

Method: Partition cancellation by workflow and branch/PR; Preserve run identity and audit records

Reported finding: Superseding runs can reduce duplicate work.

Reported metrics: {"vm_time_reduction_percent": {"free": 1.9, "paid": 4.1}}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.2.3; Table 4; PDF pp. 7: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
